flagged.evidence: The page says the normalised sinc is its own L² Fourier transform. The current `ex-shannon-reconstruction-of-a-sinc-function` Statement gives the pair sinc and the interval indicator, and Verification 1.1 derives that transform. At t=3/2, sinc is nonzero on a neighbourhood while the indicator vanishes, so the L² classes differ.

The page attributes the discrepancy to boundary double-counting and says the theorem’s two-sided decay bounds are essential. The current tiling lemma says the half-open translates are pairwise disjoint. The opened L¹ warning records one contributing translate at 0, periodisation value 2π, one-sided limits 4π and 2π, and Fourier midpoint 3π: this is a jump versus assigned value, not double-counting. That example shows bare L¹ is insufficient; it does not establish necessity of these particular decay bounds.

The cited change-of-variables dependency states the formula for “every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable” function. Proof 1.1 applies [F2] to the complex integrand e^{2πiμ·x} without stating the extension to complex functions. Applying the formula separately to the real and imaginary parts closes this immediately, so the gap is nonfatal.

The title says “Aliasing when spectral support overlaps a reciprocal translate” without requiring positive-measure overlap. For h=1 and E=[0,1], E∩(E+1)={1}, a null set; no nonzero L² class can be supported on that singleton. The Remark’s witness requires positive-measure overlap, as does its proof, so the title includes the endpoint-touching case that supplies no L² alias.
